Start with the expanded examples. Open further examples for options and alternative R approaches.

estat

Coefficient of variation of a survey mean

Stata 

estat cv

R survey 

100 * survey::cv(survey::svymean(~y, des))

Differs from Stata Coefficient of variation as a percentage: 100*SE(estimate)/estimate, matching Stata estat cv. The fitted quantity here is the design-weighted mean y; unstable when its mean is near zero.

Stata reference · R reference

svy

Survey mean with BRR replicate variance

Stata 

svy brr: mean y

R survey 

{ reps <- survey::as.svrepdesign(des, type = "BRR"); survey::svymean(~y, reps) }

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Point means agree with sampling weights; replication variance depends on the chosen scheme.

Stata reference · R reference

Stata reference · R reference

Survey subpopulation mean

Stata 

svy, subpop(if group==1): mean y

R survey 

survey::svymean(~y, subset(des, group == "1"))

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Subset the design, preserving the sampling structure, rather than rebuilding a design after filtering.

Stata reference · R reference

Survey gamma log-link model

Stata 

svy: glm y x, family(gamma) link(log)

R survey 

{ fit <- survey::svyglm(y ~ x, des, family = stats::Gamma(link = "log")); fit$df.residual <- survey::degf(des); fit }

Differs from Stata fit carries the full sampling design and sandwich covariance. For Stata-style coefficient tests use summary(fit, df.resid=survey::degf(des)); the displayed code sets that reference in the fitted object. Quasi families avoid noninteger-weight warnings.

Stata reference · R reference

Survey proportion interval using logit

Stata 

svy: proportion yes

R survey 

survey::svyciprop(~yes, des, method = "logit", level = .95)

Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Different interval constructions are intentional alternatives; match Stata's selected transformation.

Stata reference · R reference

Survey proportion interval using xlogit

Stata 

svy: proportion yes, citype(logit)

R survey 

survey::svyciprop(~yes, des, method = "xlogit", level = .95)

Stata citype(logit) and survey xlogit transform the design-based mean and its variance. Use design degrees of freedom. This is the positive category only; factor-based svymean returns all categories.

Design-based categorical association: F

Stata 

svy: tabulate group yes, pearson

R survey 

survey::svychisq(~group + yes, des, statistic = "F")

Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Rao-Scott and Wald choices have distinct reference distributions; choose the intended test explicitly.

Stata reference · R reference

Design-based categorical association: adjWald

Stata 

svy: tabulate group yes, wald

R survey 

survey::svychisq(~group + yes, des, statistic = "adjWald")

Select the stated Stata Wald option, not pearson. survey Wald gives the unadjusted design Wald F; adjWald uses its small-design-df adjustment.

svyset

Independent unequal-probability sample

Stata 

svyset [pw=w]

R survey

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Survey objects carry design metadata; do not substitute ordinary regression weights.

Poststratify survey weights to population category totals

Stata 

svyset psu [pw=w], strata(stratum) poststrata(group) postweight(pop)

R survey 

survey::postStratify(des, ~group, population = population)

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Population categories must cover the sample; weighting adjustments are part of the variance design.

Stata reference · R reference

Rake sample weights to known category margins

Stata 

svyset psu [pw=w], strata(stratum) rake(ibn.group, totals(20 30, copy) noconstant)

R survey 

survey::rake(des, sample.margins = list(~group), population.margins = list(population))

Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Survey calibration workflow; Stata's exact calibration syntax depends on svyset options/version.

Stata reference · R reference

Fay balanced repeated replication

Stata 

svyset psu [pw=w], strata(stratum) vce(brr) fay(.3)

R survey 

survey::as.svrepdesign(des, type = "Fay", fay.rho = .3)

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Match Fay's perturbation parameter and replicate scaling conventions.
